summary: The driver now halts the run when a task's second consecutive blocked outcome carries no change (outside .loop/state/) since its first blocked attempt, surfacing the first diagnosis in the halt warning and the run-end report; a run where something changed between attempts still retries and re-evaluates the rule on the next pair.
verified: bash .loop/tests/scenarios/42-repeat-blocked-halts.sh && .loop/tests/run-all.sh && uv run pytest -q -- all green: 45 passed in run-all.sh (was 44), 40 passed in pytest; ran the exact T8 verify string from state.json directly and it exits 0.
notes: Two new per-task fields on state.json's tasks, .blocked_head and .blocked_summary, added and read only by run.sh (not part of the planner's contract, not read by render-plan.sh or runstat): blocked_head is `git rev-parse HEAD` captured right before the iteration's own commit, the moment an outcome is blocked; blocked_summary is that iteration's masked summary. On the NEXT iteration for the same task, if outcome is blocked again, the driver diffs prev blocked_head..current HEAD (both still pre-commit at that point) and drops anything under .loop/state/ -- if what's left is empty, nothing changed since the first attempt, and the run halts (new status repeat_blocked, exit 8) surfacing blocked_summary from the FIRST attempt, not the one just run. If the diff is non-empty, or this is the task's first-ever blocked outcome, the driver just updates blocked_head/blocked_summary and continues -- the pair is re-evaluated fresh next time. On any non-blocked outcome (done/gate_fail/review_fail) both fields are deleted, breaking the chain. Deliberately keyed on the TASK, not on 'the iteration immediately before this one': the brief's own item-7 prose says 'the previous iteration FOR this same task', so a different ready task worked in between does not reset the chain, and the chain also survives a resumed run because it lives in state.json rather than iterations.jsonl (which run.sh truncates every run). This does cost 1-2 extra `git` invocations, but only on the (exceptional) blocked path, never on a normal iteration. Scenario 11-stall.sh had two blocked iterations with literally nothing else in the tree changing, which would now trip this rule before the old stall counter -- gave its stub a per-attempt marker file so something always changes and the scenario keeps exercising the stall halt it exists for, per the acceptance criterion. Exit code 8 and status name 'repeat_blocked' are both new; picked 8 since 0-7 were taken, and documented the new row in .loop/README.md, .loop/manual.md and B008-driver-in-python.md's 'exit codes are the contract, unchanged' list (which needed the addition to stay accurate for whenever that Python-port brief is actually worked). Left .loop/amend.sh untouched -- an operator's `amend.sh reset` doesn't clear blocked_head/blocked_summary, so a reset-without-any-other-change would still read as 'nothing changed' on the next blocked attempt and could halt again after one iteration instead of two; amend.sh is not in this task's files and the acceptance criteria don't cover that path, so I left it rather than guessing at scope.
